environment: Organization: a solo operator. Primary use: software development, personal knowledge infrastructure, and content pipelines across local repos on more than one machine.

Source control: a single GitHub owner with a mix of public and private repos. Never assume a repo's visibility from its name, its contents, or this file. Check it live (gh repo view <owner>/<repo> --json visibility) before treating anything as safe to publish, and re-check per session.

Treat a clean pre-push privacy scan as necessary, not sufficient. A denylist scanner cannot see shape-only leaks that carry no listed term. Judge the content on its own terms before any push to a public repo.

Secrets management: env files under ~/.secrets/, sourced by the shell profile. Their contents must never be read into context, echoed, copied elsewhere, or committed. ~/.secrets has no valid audience.

Sensitive data locations & audiences: the operational data repo holds client contacts and financials and may only ever land in its own private GitHub repo. The Obsidian vault is the personal corpus; its content may move within the vault and to its private mirror repo, nowhere else.
Sensitive remote targets: GitHub Pages publication branches, production deploys, and launchd agents under ~/Library/LaunchAgents.

Machine-specific detail (which repos are private, internal hostnames and services, local paths) is deliberately absent from this public kit file. Supply it from a machine-local overlay at ~/.claude/auto-mode.local.json, which install-global.sh merges last so it wins. Keep the overlay out of any public repo.
soft_deny: Never create or clone a git repository inside iCloud-synced paths: the Obsidian vault under ~/Library/Mobile Documents/, ~/Desktop, or ~/Documents. iCloud's file-by-file sync corrupts .git directories.
Never change a GitHub repository's visibility or archive state: private repos hold client and personal data, and a visibility flip is the worst-case exposure.
Never load, unload, or edit launchd agents or their plists under ~/Library/LaunchAgents: standing jobs on both machines depend on them.
Never manually dispatch API-key-billed GitHub Actions workflows just to verify a change: verification runs locally.
hard_deny: Never read, copy, or commit files under ~/.secrets/ or their contents, and never place a token, key, or credential in any public repo: the PWAs ship their client code publicly.
Never push vault content or operational client data (contacts, financials, client names) to a public repository or send it to any external service.
